hero_headline: Know who owns it, what the record shows, and where the risk sits.
hero_subheadline: Certified Professional Landmen in Duncansville, PA. Title, leasing and due diligence for companies, and plain answers for landowners and heirs.
value_paragraph:
**No hand-offs.** The landman who searches the courthouse record is the one who writes your report and takes your call.

**No guessing.** Every report says what the record shows, what it does not, and what it would take to close the gap.
team_intro: Every call and every report comes from one of the two Certified Professional Landmen who run the firm.
regions_note: Select a basin or a shaded state to see the plays worked there.
regions_hint: Shaded states mark completed project work. Available nationwide.

regions.name: Appalachian Basin
regions.summary: Home basin for the firm. Stacked Marcellus and Utica development over some of the oldest and most fragmented mineral title in the country. Heirship research, record gaps, and century-old severances are common here.

plays.name: Marcellus Shale
plays.definition: The largest natural gas field in the United States, centered in Pennsylvania and West Virginia.

plays.name: Utica Shale
plays.definition: A deeper play lying beneath the Marcellus, productive for gas, condensate, and oil, particularly in eastern Ohio.

plays.name: Clinton / Medina
plays.definition: Shallow conventional sandstones across eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania with more than a century of production history.

plays.name: Chattanooga Shale
plays.definition: A Devonian shale across Tennessee and the southern Appalachians, developed both conventionally and unconventionally.

regions.name: Gulf Coast Basin
regions.summary: The firm's longest track record. Deep gas development in the Haynesville and Bossier, oil in the Tuscaloosa Marine Shale, and long-established conventional production along the coast. Salt-dome geology and fragmented ownership are common.

plays.name: Haynesville Shale
plays.definition: A deep, high-pressure dry gas play across northwest Louisiana and East Texas, and one of the largest gas producers in the country.

plays.name: Bossier
plays.definition: A gas-bearing interval stacked above the Haynesville, frequently developed alongside it in East Texas and North Louisiana.

plays.name: Tuscaloosa Marine Shale
plays.definition: An oil-prone shale running across central Louisiana and southwest Mississippi, commonly abbreviated TMS.

plays.name: Eagle Ford Shale
plays.definition: A South Texas oil, condensate, and gas play running in a band from the Mexican border northeast toward East Texas.

plays.name: East Texas Basin
plays.definition: A long-producing conventional basin, home to the historic East Texas Oil Field and multiple stacked targets still developed today.

plays.name: Gulf Coast Trend
plays.definition: The onshore coastal belt across Texas, Louisiana, and Mississippi, where shallow conventional production and salt-dome structures dominate.

regions.name: Permian Basin
regions.summary: The largest oil-producing basin in the United States, covering more than 75,000 square miles across West Texas and southeast New Mexico. Oil sits in several stacked layers in the Midland and Delaware sub-basins, so ownership that changes with depth is a routine title issue here.

plays.name: Midland Sub-basin
plays.definition: The eastern half of the Permian, where the Spraberry and Wolfcamp benches are developed in tight, heavily leased sections.

plays.name: Delaware Sub-basin
plays.definition: The deeper western half of the Permian, running into southeast New Mexico with thicker Bone Spring and Wolfcamp targets.

regions.name: Michigan Basin
regions.summary: A bowl-shaped basin under Michigan's Lower Peninsula that produces from several stacked layers. Its shallow Antrim gas was some of the first shale gas developed commercially in the country.

plays.name: Antrim Shale
plays.definition: A shallow biogenic gas play in the northern Michigan Basin, and one of the first commercially developed shale gas plays in the United States.

plays.name: Northern Michigan Conventional
plays.definition: Niagaran pinnacle reef targets developed across the northern Lower Peninsula, with the Trenton-Black River (Albion-Scipio) trend to the south.

regions.name: Pacific Northwest
regions.summary: Renewable energy land work. Utility-scale solar and wind siting involves surface use agreements, setbacks, and long-term option periods, along with transmission and interconnection right-of-way.

plays.name: Solar & Wind Lease Acquisition
plays.definition: Option and lease packages assembled across contiguous surface tracts for utility-scale renewable siting.

plays.name: Right-of-Way Corridors
plays.definition: Transmission and interconnection routing, negotiated tract by tract to connect generation to the grid.

services_intro: Six kinds of land work, from one family's inherited tract to multi-county leasing programs and acquisition due diligence.

cta.headline: Not sure what you own? We can find out.
cta.text: Send the letter you received, or a county and a tract list. We will tell you what the record shows and what it will take.

stats.label: Combined years in oil and gas
stats.detail: Petro Land Ventures has worked files since January 2005, and each of us has more than 20 years in the business.

stats.label: Certified Professional Landmen
stats.detail: The highest credential the American Association of Professional Landmen issues for title and leasing work.

sample_feature.label: Sample Work
sample_feature.headline: See the Work Before You Call
sample_feature.text: We published a complete sample file: a runsheet (a list of every deed, will and lease in the chain), an ownership report, a lease acquisition report, and a supplemental report that resolves an heirship. It is fictional and annotated, so you can see how the work reads whether you run a land department or own forty acres.
